text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military mission to Zaire on hold: Canada, allies reconsider need for troops as refugees stream back to Rwanda.
- Reunions help ease refugees' suffering: Teen's ordeal ends back home.
- Close native cash gap now, report to urge: Commission wants federal spending on Indians $1-billion higher by 2003.
- Fetal tissue used to reverse blindness: Procedure restores partial vision for some, raises ethical questions.
- New Democrats gain going into next election: Liberals comfortably ahead, but their chief rivals vary from region to region.
- Hype fuels Telekom offering: Worldwide interest in German privatization as pricing unveiled for today's IPO launch.
- Natural gas shares spark stock markets.
- USAir faces a familiar hurdle: cut costs or crash: Deal with employees one of many issues confronting airline.
- Ottawa out on legal limb over DTH TV: Some say the government is usurping the courts when it says those who buy U.S. grey market service are breaking the law.
- U.S. phone companies send money to Cuba: Cash used to upgrade communist island's creaking telephone system.
- Canadian Airlines directors quit over liability concerns.
